title: Linjiang
capsule: The Kingdom of Linjiang was one of the Eighteen Kingdoms Xiang Yu established in 206 BC, granted to Gong Ao, a general who had served the Chu rebel cause, with territory along the middle Yangzi centered near modern Jiangling in Hubei. It was a comparatively minor fief within Xiang Yu's settlement, overshadowed by neighboring Western Chu and Jiujiang. Linjiang outlasted most of its peers: Gong Ao died in 204 BC and his son Gong Wei held out until 202 BC, when Han forces captured him after Xiang Yu's fall and folded the kingdom's middle-Yangzi territory into the new Han empire.
